data.completion_memo: W4 complete. Full built-in tool matrix (read/search/list/grep/edit/write/shell/python/todo/web_search/web_fetch) wired into the agent loop with frozen settings-driven bindings, exact configuration contracts (validate_implemented_contract == freeze_configuration), capability descriptors with correct side-effect classes, and settlement through the durable broker. Approval path: PerInvocation bindings for edit/write/shell/python suspend the Run with a durable ToolApprovalChallengeV1 (decision id, invocation id, nonce, TTL, capability id, bounded summary); the approval command applies approve/reject through pipeline.resume_approval — approve executes the exact original invocation once (broker resolve_approval → DispatchReady), reject returns a denied is_error result and the model loop continues; decisions are single-use and idempotent reapplication errors. Suspend/resume replays restore the graph-pass prefix (PendingGraphPassStateV1.agent_loop) so no model or tool work recomputes, and restart recovery reads the same stored pending approval. Expiry is enforced by the broker (nonce + expires_epoch_millis) with unit coverage in trusted-core; a live pipeline-level expiry test is impractical at the production TTL and is covered at that layer. Tools: list (glob ≤1000 entries mtime-sorted), grep (regex ≤512 matches), write (full content), edit (old_string/new_string over atomic content-hash edit) — the Windows parent-directory sync bug (Dir::open on a directory) that made every edit/write fail with Access denied was found and fixed (cfg(unix) fsync, cap-std rename), shell/python bounded host execution, todo (run-local ordered snapshot committed as pipeline.todo-state and surfaced as a durable tool.todo timeline fact via SimpleChatPipelinePort::run_todo_state), web_search (DuckDuckGo HTML parse ≤8 results) and web_fetch (HTTPS 1MiB/32KiB bounds). Integration tests added: pipeline-level tool-approval suspend → approve edits the file (activity completed, observed result echoes oldString/newString), reject leaves the file untouched (activity denied), todo end-to-end records run-local state, and the seeded Standard Agent workflow (input → plan → agent with 7 approval-free tools → output → wait) runs end to end through the graph pass. Host-level list/grep/write/edit coverage added to milestone_05 (platform-aware root-swap assertion: Unix detects identity swap, Windows pins the root via the share-mode handle), WebTools unit tests with a fake transport (bounds, cancellation, HTTPS-only, truncation, DuckDuckGo parsing, plain-text extraction), and settings_diagnostics probes for list/grep/write/todo/web (web performs a live bounded HTTPS round trip). Cross-cutting Windows platform fixes found by the QA gates: aworkit-process directory fsync now uses FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS with write access (FlushFileBuffers), aworkit-process IPC enforces deadlines on Windows via nonblocking named-pipe poll loops (interprocess rejects OS timeouts), local-store lock contention now compares fs2::lock_contended_error (Windows maps ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION to Uncategorized, not WouldBlock), and the milestone plugin fixture resolves PATH-relative interpreters to absolute identities. Verification: desktop suite 145 lib tests + 2 integration tests green (exit 0); aworkit-capability-host all targets green (lib 9, milestone_05 6, milestone_09 13, plus registry/extension/protocol suites); aworkit-process 6/6; remaining local-store Windows failures (22 tests across artifacts/ledger/projections/storage: open-handle delete/rename sharing violations and the SQLite backup Access denied) are being fixed by a dedicated subagent for the W8 QA gate — they are platform porting, not W4 tool behavior. Known boundary documented in the design: graph workflows binding edit/write/shell/python require the per-invocation approval, which is the intended UX.
data.description: Wire the full built-in tool set into the agent loop with a real approval path. (1) Implement the approval flow: approval-requiring tool calls suspend the Run in awaiting_approval with a durable approval.requested event (decision id, tool id, bounded payload summary); the user sends the approval command (approve/reject); approve executes the exact original invocation once, reject returns a denied result; decisions are single-use, TTL-bounded, and survive restart via the existing pending-effect reconciliation. (2) Tool implementation: add tool.files.list (glob, ≤1000 entries, mtime-sorted), tool.files.grep (regex, ≤512 matches, bounded file set), tool.files.write (full content, approval), tool.files.edit as old_string/new_string replace over the host's atomic content-hash edit (approval), tool.shell.host and tool.python.host wired with bounded time/output and cleared environments (approval), tool.todo (run-local plan/task list with create/update/merge semantics, committed as todo events, rendered as a live plan card), tool.web_search (HTTPS provider, ≤8 results with title/snippet/url), tool.web_fetch (HTTPS, 1 MiB download, 32 KiB extracted text). All tools: frozen settings-driven bindings, capability descriptors with correct side-effect classes, settled through the durable broker, bounded inputs/outputs, exact activity evidence. Fix the currently-rejected edit/shell/python paths. Output: working tools with Rust integration tests including approval accept/reject/expiry and crash-resume.
data.title: W4 — Approval path plus the complete built-in tool set (list, grep, write, edit, shell, python, todo, web_search, web_fetch)
